The circles $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $r=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ intersect at points $O$ and $A,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates of the point $A?$
question.worked_solution:
First of all, we notice from the graph that the origin $O$ is an obvious first point of intersection.

To find the second point of intersection, we set the equations of the curves equal to each other and solve for $\theta :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =-\frac{2}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the solution $\theta ={315}^{∘}$ in the $4$th quadrant.

Now, we use the equation $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ to find the $r$-coordinate of the point $A:$  

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡({315}^{∘}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of the point $A$ are 

$\,$ $(r,\theta )=(\sqrt{2},{315}^{∘}).$
